title: AI Coding Toolkit System Dataflow
description: A very-high-level graph of how data moves through a system. It can explain a feature's user workflows or visualize system dataflow for general system understanding, focusing on system boundaries, persistent state, and critical data processing.

schemaVersion.description: Version of the System Dataflow schema used by this document.

stage.description: The development stage represented by the dataflow: proposed behavior during high-level design or implemented behavior during code review.

feature.description: Name of the feature whose behavior the dataflow explains.

diffHunks.description: Unified diff hunks that provide implementation evidence for nodes and relationships in a code-review dataflow.

nodes.description: User inputs and outputs, external dependencies, system inputs and outputs, persistent state, static data, and critical data processing in the dataflow.

relationships.description: Directed data flows connecting the nodes.

diffHunk.description: One exact unified diff hunk from the current working tree compared with HEAD.

id.description: Unique identifier referenced by nodes and relationships in this document.

file.description: Repository-relative path of the file containing the hunk.

patch.description: Exact unified diff hunk, including its @@ header.

node.description: A high-level component in the dataflow. Its type determines whether relationships may enter it, leave it, or both.

type.description: The node's semantic role in the system dataflow.

oneOf.description: Data or an action supplied by a user through a user interface. Dataflow relationships may leave this node but may not enter it.

Information presented to a user through a user interface. Dataflow relationships may enter this node but may not leave it. Represent a UI component separately as user input and user output when it serves both roles.
A service, datastore, or other system outside the modeled system boundary that receives requests or data and supplies responses or data. Dataflow relationships may enter and leave this node.
Data sent into the modeled feature or system by an external system. Dataflow relationships may leave this node but may not enter it.
A final output sent by the modeled feature or system to an external system. Dataflow relationships may enter this node but may not leave it.

Persistent state read or updated by the dataflow, including but not limited to instance, static, or global variables and browser, file, database, or object storage. Dataflow relationships may enter and leave this node.

Fixed data used by the system that is not changed by the represented dataflow, such as configuration, constants, schemas, or static lookup data. Dataflow relationships may leave this node but may not enter it.
Critical or non-trivial data processing or an algorithm that transforms data in the dataflow. Dataflow relationships may enter and leave this node.

name.description: Unique name of the node within the document; relationships use this value as the node identifier.

description.description: What the node represents and the responsibility it has in the dataflow.

medium.description: The concrete medium through which the node exists or operates, such as a UI, database, file, browser storage, or external service. For data processing, this is the programming language

location.description: The concrete system location, such as a UI component name, storage location, external service URI, or class and method name. Do not use a source-code file or line location.

changeType.description: How the node changes relative to the comparison baseline.

diffHunkIds.description: Diff hunks that establish this changed node's behavior.

algorithm.description: The critical processing logic as pseudocode or actual source code.

relationship.description: A directed flow of data between two nodes.

id.description: Unique identifier for the relationship within the document.

from.description: Name of the node that supplies the data.

to.description: Name of the node that receives the data.

type.description: Kind of relationship between the nodes.

changeType.description: How the relationship changes relative to the comparison baseline.

diffHunkIds.description: Diff hunks that show this changed data transfer.

data.description: The description of the data transferred between the nodes, including a short name and the shape of the data.

purpose.description: Why this dataflow is needed and what system behavior it enables.
